placeKinds:
Fewer places, each worth a conversation (Josh, 2026-10-27; docs/adventures.md). Every kind of place appears at most as often as listed; never two places a learner would talk about the same way.

Daily life:
- 1 or 2 bars/cafés at most - morning coffee, the daily touchpoint
- no bakeries (Josh: "the conversation is poor")
- 1 gelateria at most, and only where the city is known for it
- 1 market - produce and local food, with a vendor who has something to say

Eating:
- 1 place to eat that only this city has (Bologna's osteria where people bring their own food, Rome's trattoria, Palermo's street food)

Public places, where people are rather than serve:
- 1 major landmark
- 1 church or cultural site
- 1 piazza or park

Practical:
- 1 everyday errand (pharmacy, tabaccheria, post office, hardware shop)
- 1 transport hub (the train station; it's how the learner travels)

What makes this city itself (2 or 3):
- Places only this city has (a gondola workshop in Venice, the presepe street in Naples, a leather workshop in Florence), or a place where something is happening (a flea market at dawn, a choir rehearsal, a dig)
- At least one person with something to show: a scholar, a priest, a museum guide, a professor, a journalist, an archaeologist

Who is where:
- At a business, someone who works there (the owner fits too).
- Customers, students and passers-by only in public places (piazzas, parks, churches, steps, stops), never in a shop with nothing to sell.
- Every person has a reason to be at their place today (the `here` line).

Kinds: one name per kind, lowercase, the same across cities ("bar", "market", "train-station", "pharmacy", "landmark", "church", "piazza", "park"); the place's own name says the rest.
placePrompt: Soft pastel sketch on white paper of [the place]. [Colours, light, mood]. Warm colors, textured, inviting.
portraitPrompt: Pen and ink portrait on white paper of [the person]. Minimal watercolor wash in [a few colours]. Detailed linework, personal. The subject is a [woman/man].

placeStyles.roma-nuova: Fine-line pen drawing on white paper, precise thin black lines, flat light colour fills
placeStyles.napoli: Pencil and watercolour on textured paper, loose hand-drawn line, sunlit, in the real colours of Naples: plaster house fronts in warm yellow, ochre, salmon pink and terracotta, green shutters, a strip of blue sky. Dense and crowded, as Naples is: tall buildings close together, balconies crammed with plants and laundry, cables overhead, scooters squeezed everywhere, and many people close to the viewer, talking, carrying bags, gesturing. One strong accent of colour that belongs to this place itself (its awning, its tiles, its shutters or its food), not the same in every picture; scooters in ordinary dull colours, not a red Vespa. Lived-in and a little worn, with soft shadows, not grimy. No street shrine unless the scene asks for one. Not a clean digital illustration, not a tourist postcard, not HDR
placeStyles.palermo: Pencil and watercolour on textured paper, loose hand-drawn line, sunlit, in the real colours and architecture of Palermo: honey and golden sandstone, faded baroque palazzi in cream, ochre and pale rose, grey stone doorways, wrought-iron balconies with curved bellied railings, tall wooden shutters in brown or green, a palm tree here and there. Church domes only where the scene names a church. Strong dry Sicilian light, a deep blue sky, warmer and more open than Naples. Busy and lived-in, with many people close to the viewer, talking, shopping, carrying bags. Fruit crates and three-wheeled vans only where the scene asks for them. One strong accent of colour that belongs to this place itself (its awning, its tiles, its food or its dome), not the same in every picture; scooters in ordinary dull colours. A little worn, with soft shadows, not grimy. Not a clean digital illustration, not a tourist postcard, not HDR
placeStyles.venezia: Bold watercolour on white paper, saturated colour: strong primaries, brick red, saffron and ochre house fronts, green shutters, washes laid on wet and bright, deep shadows, hard Venetian sunlight. Show water only if the scene is on a canal; streets and squares stay on dry stone. Now and then, not every time: a few pigeons, a striped mooring pole, a boat or a sail

placeFraming.about: Where the camera stands (Josh, 2026-10-27, from the Naples style test: "why not vary them"). Squares, markets and landmarks are seen wide; every other place takes the next view in turn, in the city file's order, so neighbours in the feed differ.
placeFraming.wide: Seen from a step back: the place as part of its street or piazza, with depth, sky and the city around it.
views: Seen from the street, straight on and close: the shop front fills the picture, the name readable, the counter visible through the open doorway, people at the counter and in front of it. The shop is the ground floor of a tall old building, with flats and balconies above it.
Seen from across a narrow street: the place in the middle of the picture between its neighbours, the shop the ground floor of a tall old building, people and scooters passing in front.
Seen on its street corner, where two streets meet at an angle: the place on the corner, both streets running away on either side.
Seen from inside, from the customer's side of the counter: the person who works there facing you, the street visible through the open door behind.
Seen looking along the street: the place's front on one side in the near half of the picture, the street running away into the distance, crowded and busy.

placeRules: No other words anywhere: no dates, no neighbourhood or city names, no slogans, no prices, no brand names or logos. Contemporary Italy: today's clothes and objects, everyday life. Shops, bars and restaurants are on the ground floor of a continuous row of apartment buildings, as in an Italian city, never a separate small building or kiosk. Keep the main scene in the centre; nothing important near the edges.
placeStylesNote: Roma nuova (2026-10-22, docs/rome-redo.md): place prompt = city style + scene + its name as the only sign + placeRules (scripts/lib/place-prompt.mjs), as Mexico does. Cities without a style keep their full imagePrompt. Napoli (2026-10-27, from Josh's Spanish Quarter photos; three test rounds): its style plus placeFraming, close for shops and food, wide for squares, markets and landmarks.
